brief: MRB argues the Fed is already behind the curve on inflation and should hike regardless of what August core CPI shows. Core PCE inflation reaccelerated from 2.6% in April to 3.3% in July, and Taylor-rule estimates put the policy rate at least a percentage point too low. A benign August print would not confirm a turn: the three-month annualized core PCE rate was 3% in July, trimmed-mean and median measures are elevated, and about 60% of core PCE components run above 3%. Core goods may ease as tariff effects fade, but housing disinflation is bottoming and core services excluding housing are trending up. AI capex is pushing PCE gains via software/accessories inflation, though a coming BEA methodology change will lower that contribution; October CPI will step up regardless as a shutdown-related base effect drops out. Wage growth's underlying trend has bottomed and the job-switcher wage premium is back, risking a services-inflation reacceleration. MRB expects more than two hikes are needed; the bond market has moved from pricing two hikes to three. Delaying risks the Fed's, and Warsh's, credibility.
